raw_content: {"cards":[{"title":"Technical SEO on Shopify: Audit Order and Purpose","summary":"Run a three-step Shopify technical SEO audit (manual, crawl, Search Console) as the foundation before content or link work.","use_when":"Before investing in content marketing or link building for your store; when organic rankings are stagnant and you don't know if the technical foundation is broken.","steps":["Understand the mechanism: Google spends a limited crawl budget per site, so cleaning up duplicates and low-value pages lowers the 'cost of retrieval' and improves your odds of ranking.","Step 1 - Manually review the store for the known Shopify issue classes: product URL duplication from collection paths, auto-generated tag/vendor/type pages, unredirected deleted products, variant duplication, missing structured data.","Step 2 - Crawl the whole site with a crawler such as Sitebulb, using the Chrome (JS-rendering) crawler and a mobile user agent since Google uses mobile-first indexing. Enable structured data checks in crawl settings.","Step 3 - Open Google Search Console and review Page Indexing for 404s, 'crawled - currently not indexed,' robots.txt blocks, and the Shopping/Enhancements structured data reports.","Prioritize critical and high-severity crawl issues first, then work down the list. Fix redirects on unintended 404s (301 to the relevant live page) to recover traffic and preserve link equity."],"caveats":["Presenter's opinion: technical SEO is the mandatory first step; skipping it undermines even excellent content and backlinks.","Sitebulb and GSC interfaces change - verify current menu names.","Large stores with thousands of pages are most affected, but small stores still benefit."],"tags":["search","technical-seo","site-audit","search-console","crawlability","indexing","shopify"]},{"title":"Fix Shopify Product URL Duplication (Within-Collection Paths)","summary":"Remove the within-collection URL parameter in Shopify theme code so product links always resolve to the canonical /products/ URL.","use_when":"When auditing technical SEO on a Shopify store and product URLs appear as /collections/x/products/y when navigated from a collection.","steps":["Navigate to a product via two different collections and confirm the URL changes (e.g., .../collections/healthy-beef-jerky/products/... vs .../collections/jerky/products/...).","View source and locate the canonical tag: Shopify usually still points canonical to the clean /products/handle URL, so Google needs to reconcile multiple URLs and duplicates waste crawl budget.","Go to Shopify admin > Online Store > Edit code, open Snippets and find the product grid snippet (commonly main-collection-product-grid.liquid or another file with 'grid' in the name).","Search the snippet for 'within_collection' and delete that parameter, then save. Repeat for all instances of within_collection across theme files.","Note that some newer themes already omit this parameter - if you can't find it, no action is needed."],"caveats":["Editing this can break URL-derived breadcrumbs - see the breadcrumb meta field card.","Always back up your theme before editing; if unsure, ask a developer or AI assistant where to place code.","Remove from every occurrence, not just the first."],"tags":["search","technical-seo","url-structure","shopify","theme-code","crawlability"]},{"title":"Rebuild Shopify Breadcrumbs With a Meta Field After URL Fix","summary":"Shopify builds breadcrumbs from the URL path, so fixing product URLs breaks them - store collection links in a breadcrumb meta field and render from that.","use_when":"After removing the within_collection parameter (or any time breadcrumbs on product/collection pages disappear or show wrong hierarchy).","steps":["In Shopify admin, go to Content > Metaobjects > Manage definitions, select Products, and create a new definition such as 'breadcrumb'.","Set it to global and choose type URL (avoid the collection type, which can create issues).","For each product, store the URL of the collection it belongs to in that meta field.","Modify the theme's breadcrumb section/snippet to render the link from that meta field instead of Shopify's default URL-derived breadcrumb.","This also gives manual control over what each breadcrumb says rather than relying on URL parsing."],"caveats":["Best done with at least some theme code comfort; the source suggests asking ChatGPT to help place the code if non-developer.","Best practice: same manual meta-field approach for collection pages.","Full how-to code isn't fully given here - verify instructions in current Shopify theme docs."],"tags":["search","technical-seo","breadcrumbs","shopify","theme-code","navigation"]},{"title":"No-Index Auto-Generated Tag, Vendor, Type, and Utility Pages","summary":"Shopify generates thin tag/vendor/type/utility pages that can't be customized, so set them to noindex, follow.","use_when":"When the store has many product tags (sizes, colors, skin types) or blog tags, or when GSC shows many thin/duplicate pages indexed.","steps":["Understand the issue: tags with spaces become ugly URLs, auto-generated tag pages can't have unique titles/H1s/meta descriptions, and sites with thousands of products/posts produce thousands of thin duplicate pages.","For product tags and blog tags, add the provided noindex, follow code snippet to your theme.liquid file.","For vendor and product-type pages, add the corresponding noindex, follow snippets to theme.liquid as well.","Also noindex site utility pages: all collections, all products, new products - they target no keywords and serve no SEO purpose.","Do NOT index tags you actually want: create a real dedicated collection page for that tag instead (e.g., 'moisturizers for dry skin'), so you control H1, URL, title, and content."],"caveats":["Find the correct spot in theme.liquid via a developer or AI assistant - Shopify's theme structure varies by theme.","Noindex, follow preserves link equity while preventing indexation."],"tags":["search","technical-seo","indexing","shopify","tag-pages","thin-content"]},{"title":"Custom robots.txt on Shopify: Block Low-Value Pages","summary":"Create a custom robots.txt in a Shopify template to block crawling of auto-generated, duplicate, and low-value pages.","use_when":"After you have set low-value pages to noindex, as defense-in-depth to save crawl budget from duplicate/tag/vendor churn.","steps":["Go to Shopify admin > Online Store > Edit code > Templates and click Add a new template, selecting the robots.txt template type.","Add rules blocking crawling of: all product collections, vendor pages, product type pages, product tag pages, and blog tag pages.","Replace any placeholder domain with your real domain in the snippets.","Check your current robots.txt by visiting yourdomain.com/robots.txt.","PREREQUISITE: Only block these if you already fixed the product URL duplication, since mismatched rules can create crawl problems for products."],"caveats":["Proceed with caution - the presenter explicitly warns that these rules can cause crawl issues if you don't fully understand them.","If already noindexed via other means, robots.txt changes add redundancy rather than new treatment.","Verify current Shopify template behavior against live docs before deploying."],"tags":["search","technical-seo","robots-txt","crawl-budget","shopify","indexing"]},{"title":"Manage Variant Duplication: Merge or Canonicalize","summary":"Merge low-search-volume variants into one product, or keep them but point canonical tags at the primary product URL.","use_when":"When color/size variants each create near-duplicate product listings (e.g., cotton sock green vs cotton sock black) with no distinct descriptions or search volume.","steps":["Assess whether the variant difference has meaningful search demand and whether the variant page would have genuinely unique content (description, H1, title).","Option 1 - Merge: create one Shopify product with the variants as options, keeping one URL and one content set. This keeps the site clean and avoids duplicate pages.","Option 2 - Canonicalize: create separate variant products but use a custom metafield holding the canonical URL, editable in bulk via Shopify admin (paste the primary product URL for each variant).","Or update the theme to read that canonical metafield and emit the canonical tag - ask a developer or AI assistant for placement.","Goal either way: search engines index only the primary product page while users can still browse variants."],"caveats":["Do not create separate variant pages when there is no significant search volume - that creates thin duplicates.","Presenter's judgment, not a hard benchmark; the threshold of 'significant search volume' is contextual."],"tags":["search","technical-seo","product-variants","canonical-tags","duplicate-content","shopify"]},{"title":"Redirect Deleted Products to Preserve Redirect Path and Link Equity","summary":"Never let deleted product URLs 404 - 301 redirect them to a related product or collection to keep visitors and link equity.","use_when":"Whenever a product is removed or discontinued and was previously live, especially if it received traffic or backlinks.","steps":["Before or immediately after deleting, go to Shopify admin > Online Store > Navigation > View URL redirects.","Add a redirect from the deleted product URL to a relevant replacement product or collection page - not the homepage unless nothing relevant exists.","Save the redirect.","Confirm in Google Search Console that old URLs return 301s rather than 404s.","This preserves link equity from any external links to the deleted product and prevents bad user experiences."],"caveats":["A 404 does not automatically harm rankings, but redirecting relevant pages preserves equity and UX per the source's practice.","Redirect to genuinely relevant pages; redirecting everything to the homepage is noted as suboptimal."],"tags":["search","technical-seo","redirects","link-equity","shopify","user-experience"]},{"title":"Remove Pages from Shopify Sitemaps Correctly (Avoid the Hidden SEO Trap)","summary":"Shopify requires manual sitemap exclusion, and the hidden SEO checkbox also forces noindex, nofollow - use the theme meta tag instead.","use_when":"When you canonicalize or want to exclude pages from the sitemap without preventing them from ranking (e.g., variant or parameter pages).","steps":["Unlike WordPress, Shopify does NOT automatically remove canonicalized/noindexed pages from the sitemap.","Shopify exposes a hidden SEO field for products/pages (accessible via a special admin URL path; verify current mechanics). Setting its toggle to true removes the URL from the sitemap.","CAUTION: setting the hidden SEO toggle also sets the page to noindex, nofollow - bad if you only wanted sitemap exclusion.","To bypass that side effect, edit theme.liquid, find the relevant section, and replace it with the provided code snippet so the page is excluded from the sitemap without noindex, nofollow.","Test by requesting the sitemap after the change."],"caveats":["Editing theme code without developer experience risks breaking structured output; the presenter advises caution.","Shopify admin internals change - validate the current hidden SEO field behavior before relying on it."],"tags":["search","technical-seo","sitemap","shopify","indexing","theme-code"]},{"title":"Implement Product, Article, and Breadcrumb Structured Data","summary":"Verify and enrich schema so products show price, ratings, shipping, and returns in search results, and breadcrumbs show hierarchy.","use_when":"When you want rich snippets for product and blog listings, or when auditing technical SEO to ensure schema is valid.","steps":["Product schema: most Shopify themes include basic product schema, but verify it is actually output and includes the key properties your theme supports (price, availability, ratings, shipping/return info where relevant).","Article schema for blog posts: check the theme's default output and verify key properties are present; blog articles pulling in rich results supports content-led SEO.","BreadcrumbList schema: check the theme's breadcrumbs.liquid snippet under Snippets to ensure it emits BreadcrumbList markup that reflects your site hierarchy.","Use GSC's Shopping/Enhancements structured data report and a crawler's structured data check to catch errors (often trivial, like a missing comma).","If implementation is beyond you, get a developer - the payoff is richer SERP presentation and clearer context for Google."],"caveats":["Exact key property lists weren't enumerated in the source; verify against schema.org and current Google rich results requirements.","Schema issues can silently lose rich snippet eligibility."],"tags":["search","technical-seo","structured-data","schema","rich-snippets","shopify"]},{"title":"Posture Site Speed: Avoid Bloat Rather Than Optimize","summary":"Shopify is fast out of the box; site speed work mostly means avoiding heavy themes, oversized images, and unused/unconditional apps.","use_when":"When store pages feel slow, mobile conversion lags, or before adding new apps, sliders, or hero assets.","steps"["Acknowledge the baseline: Shopify's hosting, browser caching, and CDN make a bare store fast. Speed degrades from added factors.","Diagnose with Google PageSpeed Insights to see actual bottlenecks and third-party impact.","Apply the fixes in priority order: lightweight theme, image format/size optimization, lazy loading, removing dead app code, conditional app scripts, minification.","Treat speed as both a conversion lever (bounce/abandonment) and a (modest) ranking signal, per the source's cited data."],"caveats":["The source cites Semrush/Search Engine Watch graphics for speed-to-conversion and speed-to-ranking relationships but reports the ranking effect as slight.","Precise speed benchmarks vary by store and connection; no universal target is established here."],"tags":["search","site-speed","conversion-optimization","shopify","pagespeed","diagnostics"]},{"title":"Choose Lightweight Themes and Cut Hero/Grid Bloat","summary":"Prefer lean themes (Dawn free; Palo Alto paid) and replace sliders, carousels, and oversized grids with simpler components.","use_when":"At store build time or when auditing an existing Shopify theme that feels sluggish on mobile.","steps":["If starting fresh, choose a lightweight, efficiently coded theme: Dawn is suggested for free, Palo Alto when budget allows.","Audit an existing theme for bloat: count sliders/carousels, hero styles, and oversized product grids.","Replace a slider with a single static hero image.","Cut product carousels from large counts (the source's example: 64 items) to a manageable number (~8) if the design allows.","These structural simplifications improve speed without needing code-level optimization."],"caveats":["Theme recommendations reflect the presenter's opinion and may date; verify current theme marketplace options.","Reducing components can affect merchandising/design - balance speed with conversion needs."],"tags":["search","site-speed","theme-selection","merchandising","shopify","mobile"]},{"title":"Optimize Image Format and Compression for Speed","summary":"Use WebP/JPEG for product images, WebP/PNG for hero text graphics, SVG for logos, and auto-compress with an app.","use_when":"When preparing product photography, hero images, logos, or auditing an image-heavy collection page.","steps":["Choose format by role: WebP or JPEG for product photos; WebP for hero images and text graphics (good quality/size balance); PNG for lossless/absolute clarity; SVG for logos and icons (vector, crisp, tiny).","Compress existing images app-side: the source uses Crush Pixels (Shopify app) which auto-compresses on upload, commonly cutting file sizes ~50%.","For manual compression, the source cites Crush Pics app results (nearly identical visual quality, ~50% smaller).","Resize images before upload so you never upload desktop-resolution images for mobile consumption.","Adopt srcset for responsive images: let browsers load an appropriately sized source per device - mobile loads small, high-DPI loads large."],"caveats":["Percentages cited are the presenter's example, not a guaranteed benchmark.","srcset requires theme code edits - may need a developer.","App names/features change; verify current Shopify app listings."],"tags":["search","site-speed","images","webp","shopify","core-web-vitals"]},{"title":"Lazy Load Offscreen Images on Collection Pages","summary":"Delay loading images until they approach the viewport so long product grids don't load every image up front.","use_when":"On collection/category pages with many product images (e.g., 36-grid) where only the first rows are visible at load.","steps":["Understand the mechanism: by default the browser loads every image at once, but only the first visible rows matter for initial load time.","Add the lazysizes.js library to the theme's assets folder.","Modify theme.liquid to include the lazysizes.js script.","Update image tags: replace the src attribute with data-src and add the lazyload class to the image.","Save and test on mobile - offscreen images should only load as the user scrolls."],"caveats":["Over-lazy-loading above-the-fold images can hurt LCP - do not lazy-load the hero.","Source gives one library (lazysizes); modern browsers support native loading='lazy' as an alternative to verify.","Requires theme code deployment; back up first."],"tags":["search","site-speed","lazy-loading","collections","shopify","theme-code"]},{"title":"Audit and Remove Unused App Code from Themes","summary":"Uninstalling a Shopify app often leaves its scripts behind in the theme, so sweep with PageSpeed Insights and remove orphan code.","use_when":"After uninstalling apps, or when third-party script overhead is flagged on the store.","steps":["Recognize that uninstalling an app does not always remove its code injections from the theme.","Run Google PageSpeed Insights and read the 'Reduce the impact of third-party code' findings.","Look for scripts serving from domains of apps you no longer use, and any code not serving the current setup.","Remove obsolete app code from theme files, or have a developer do it to avoid breaking live functionality.","Only install essential apps; where possible, bake functionality into theme code instead of adding another app."],"caveats":["Removing the wrong snippet can break live features - the source recommends a developer for pinpoint-safe removal.","There's no built-in Shopify 'app cleanup' guarantee; residue varies by app."],"tags":["search","site-speed","third-party-scripts","shopify","app-management","pagespeed"]},{"title":"Conditionally Load App Scripts by Page Type","summary":"Load each app's scripts only on pages where they're needed instead of sitewide via theme.liquid.","use_when":"When review widgets, zoom scripts, custom-option code, or social share buttons load on every page and slow unrelated pages.","steps":["Identify where each app's scripts currently load (typically theme.liquid sitewide).","Map scripts to pages: product previews/reviews, image zoom, custom options -> product pages only; social share buttons -> blog posts only.","In theme.liquid or relevant templates, wrap each script in a Liquid condition so it only renders on the matching template (e.g., only when template contains 'product').","Save and verify the feature still works on its intended page and no longer loads elsewhere.","If uncomfortable with code, have a developer implement the conditionals."],"caveats":["Conditional includes can break if apps assume their scripts load globally - test each feature.","Requires theme edit and periodic re-audit when apps update."],"tags":["search","site-speed","third-party-scripts","shopify","theme-code","conditional-loading"]},{"title":"Minify JavaScript and CSS to Reduce File Size","summary":"Strip comments, spacing, and line breaks from JS/CSS to shrink files and speed up loading.","use_when":"When PageSpeed or an audit shows unminified JS/CSS asset opportunities on the store.","steps":["Understand minification: remove developer-only characters (spaces, line breaks, comments) without changing functionality.","For a no-code route, use a Shopify app like File Optimizer to auto-minify assets.","For manual JS minification, use a tool such as JSCompress.","For CSS, Shopify offers a built-in route - the source notes you can convert CSS to the .doc.css form (verify current Shopify asset/SCSS handling).","Apply, then re-run PageSpeed to confirm reduced transfer sizes."],"caveats":["Keep an unminified copy for future editing.","App names and Shopify's built-in CSS handling evolve - verify current dashboard options."],"tags":["search","site-speed","minification","javascript","css","shopify"]}]}

15-SEO / search engine optimization Goes here. A comprehensive Shopify SEO playbook detailing technical SEO fixes, site speed optimization, keyword research methodologies (topical maps), site structure and navigation design, on-page optimization for collections and products, content marketing (blog strategy), and off-page SEO (backlinking, guest posting, HARO). Not here. • Configuring the backend Shopify store settings (payments, shipping, taxes) -> 05-SET • Editing the visual layout of a landing page without SEO focus -> 07-LPG

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Provides an end-to-end framework for scaling Shopify revenue through organic search, covering technical foundation, keyword strategy, and off-page link building. modules: [SEO] topics: [technical SEO, site speed, keyword research, site structure, on-page SEO, content strategy, link building] tier: 2 scope_hint: comprehensive

Topics. technical SEO / correcting Shopify’s default URL structure (removing the collection path from product URLs), managing product/blog tag indexing, utilizing custom robots.txt, handling product variants (merging vs. canonical tags), redirecting deleted products, and implementing structured data (schema); site speed / choosing lightweight themes, optimizing image formats (WebP) and sizes, implementing lazy loading, async/deferring non-essential scripts, and minifying code; keyword research / building topical maps using tools like Semrush and Keyword Cupid, prioritizing bottom-of-funnel pages via Google Search Console impressions, conducting keyword gap analysis, and matching search intent; site structure / optimizing main menus, featuring high-volume collections on the homepage, utilizing faceted navigation (with caution), and implementing breadcrumbs and related product links; on-page SEO / optimizing key elements (Title, H1, URL) for collection and product pages, adding detailed descriptions (splitting descriptions above and below grids), incorporating FAQ accordions, and leveraging rich snippets; content strategy / building topical authority through comprehensive blog content, internally linking to shopping pages, and embedding product CTAs; link building / building foundational links (citations, social profiles), executing guest posts and niche edits (prospecting, outreach, negotiation), and utilizing platforms like HARO/Connectively for PR and media backlinks.

Look for.

The URL Structure Fix: Editing the Shopify theme code (specifically the product grid snippet) to remove the within collection parameter, ensuring product URLs always point to the primary /products/product-name path rather than creating duplicate URLs with the collection path.

Topical Mapping: Building out comprehensive content covering all subtopics related to a main keyword to establish the site as an authority, enabling it to outrank larger, broader competitors like Amazon.

The "One Topic Per Page" Rule: Ensuring that no two pages on the site target the exact same keyword (keyword cannibalization), assigning distinct topics to collections, products, and blog posts based on search intent.

Guest Posting Strategy: The specific process for scraping a competitor's backlink profile using Semrush, filtering for domains with >1,000 monthly visits, and executing cold email outreach to secure contextual links.

Skip. Plugs for the agency's done-for-you services or the School community.

Scope mix. 10% baseline (basic Shopify navigation), 90% growth (advanced technical SEO, link building strategies). Volume. ~450 words.
